conventions.commits: Conventional commits with scope, e.g. `feat(core): add Swift language support with tree-sitter-swift handler (#1742)` (commit dbc2971); every commit needs a `Signed-off-by:` DCO trailer and GPG signing per the issue.
conventions.testing: Unit tests inline in languages/<lang>.rs `mod tests` (parse helper, Query::new compile check, happy path and edge case); core integration tests in crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/integration_tests.rs; MCP integration tests in crates/aptu-coder/tests/ via common::call_tool_raw and tempfile.
conventions.linting: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --locked --profile ci -- -D warnings -W clippy::cognitive_complexity; workspace lints deny unwrap_used, expect_used, undocumented_unsafe_blocks; cargo deny check advisories licenses bans; SPDX-FileCopyrightText check on every file; markdownlint on README; jscpd duplicate-code scan on crates/.
conventions.error_handling: Handlers return Option or Vec and never Result; query compile errors surface as ParserError::QueryError from parser.rs; text extraction uses get_node_text (returns Option) in languages/mod.rs, while java.rs slices raw and swift.rs uses get_node_text.

patterns: LanguageInfo registry: one match arm in get_language_info() plus one in get_ts_language(), each keyed by language name (languages/mod.rs).
Per-language module with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY as `pub const ... : &str = r"..."` (java.rs 4-37, swift.rs 6-37).
Element capture contract: a `function` capture on the outer node with `func_name` or `method_name` inside, and a `class` capture with `class_name` inside (parser_elements.rs 282-296).
Defuse capture contract: capture-name prefix write., read., or writeread. decides DefUseKind; reads at offsets already written are deduplicated (parser_elements.rs 868-890).
Inheritance handler signature fn(&Node, &str) -> Vec<String> with 'extends X' / 'implements X' strings (java.rs 131-165); swift.rs checks node.kind() first and returns empty otherwise.

Inline test structure: parse_<lang> helper, a queries_compile test calling tree_sitter::Query::new for every constant, an element happy-path test, an inheritance happy-path test and a no-inheritance test (swift.rs 78-end).
Wiring-by-example: the css integration touches workspace Cargo.toml, crate Cargo.toml, lang.rs EXTENSION_MAP, languages/mod.rs pub mod, two match arms, and the handler file.

related_issues.title: [FEATURE] Add PHP language support via tree-sitter-php grammar
related_issues.relevance: The task issue. Maintainers state they are implementing it in-house and external PRs will be closed, so this Scout output is for internal planning.

related_issues.title: feat(core): add Swift language support with tree-sitter-swift handler

related_issues.title: not fetched (referenced only in the issue)
related_issues.relevance: Issue says extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver and find_receiver_type have had no consumer since #1807, so PHP leaves them None.

constraints: Use LANGUAGE_PHP, not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY: php_only/src/node-types.json has no `text` kind, so inline HTML would produce ERROR nodes; the issue's HTML-template acceptance criterion depends on the mixed grammar.
PHP has no `identifier` node kind (absent from php/src/node-types.json); java.rs-style `(identifier)` patterns fail Query::new. Use `name`, `variable_name` and `qualified_name`.

A defuse query that fails to compile makes Query::new return ParserError::QueryError (parser.rs 159-170), which would break analysis of every .php file, so the DEFUSE pattern must be compile-tested before wiring.

DEFUSE_QUERY is Option<&'static str> in LanguageInfo, so omitting it compiles; it is required by the issue scope ('the five query constants'), by the java/swift/csharp templates, and because without it analysis returns empty (parser_elements.rs 850-852).
Inheritance must be a kind-based walk: base_clause and class_interface_clause have no field names in the grammar, so child_by_field_name('superclass') from java.rs returns None.
Workspace deny lints (unwrap_used, expect_used) apply to non-test code; use get_node_text instead of raw slicing; SPDX header required on php.rs.

New Cargo.lock entries must be at least 7 days old (AGENTS.md; .github/scripts/check-package-age.sh). The v0.25.2 tag commit is dated 2026-11-19, but the crates.io publish date was not verifiable with gh.
tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 depends only on tree-sitter-language ^0.1 at runtime (lock has 0.1.9); tree-sitter 0.27 is only a dev-dependency, so it should link against workspace tree-sitter 0.27.x.
Issue scope excludes .phtml/.inc/.module/.php5, trait use resolution, property/constant extraction, attributes and namespace aliasing; the wiring must not touch tool handlers or schemas.
README count '18 languages' (README.md line 47) is also repeated in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md line 12; the issue scopes only README.md, so the ARCHITECTURE.md edit needs an explicit decision.
Git history for the sibling integrations is partly unreadable in this clone (missing tree objects for dbc2971 and 07c50d4), so wiring facts were taken from the current tree.
test_coverage: Existing language modules each carry inline tests: java.rs has 6 (element happy path, inheritance happy path, defuse write site, receiver/function-name helpers); swift.rs has 5 (queries_compile, set_language smoke, element happy path, inheritance with and without clauses); css.rs has 3 (rule-set extraction, @import extraction, empty file). lang.rs tests cover language_for_extension happy and edge cases, with swift asserted but not css. languages/mod.rs has a registration table test (line 383-end) that lists css with (false, true). Core integration tests in crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/integration_tests.rs cover tsx, Fortran and others through analyze_file. No existing test covers the PHP mixed HTML template case; a new one is needed.

library_findings.version: 0.25.2 (latest tag v0.25.2; tag commit c1e13490, dated 2026-11-19)
library_findings.relevant_api: LANGUAGE_PHP (mixed HTML and PHP), LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY, PHP_NODE_TYPES, TAGS_QUERY; Cargo.toml: tree-sitter-language = "0.1" runtime, tree-sitter = "0.27" dev-dependency, build = bindings/rust/build.rs
library_findings.notes: Node kinds confirmed in php/src/node-types.json: class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration, function_definition, method_declaration (all with name field of kind `name`), base_clause, class_interface_clause (no field names), function_call_expression (function field), member_call_expression and nullsafe_member_call_expression and scoped_call_expression (name field), namespace_use_declaration, named_type, simple_parameter (name: variable_name), variable_name (children: name), assignment_expression (left/right), augmented_assignment_expression, update_expression (argument field). No `identifier` kind. php/grammar.js is a 3-line wrapper around common/define-grammar.js, which holds the real rules. Upstream queries/tags.scm has no enum_declaration pattern. The crates.io publish date for 0.25.2 was not verified.

Context7 (/tree-sitter/tree-sitter) confirms field-name prefix syntax and alternation. An unknown node type in a query makes Query::new return Err, which is the failure mode for a stray `(identifier)` pattern. The grammar crate's own Rust test uses the same LanguageFn constants with tree-sitter 0.27.

approaches.name: A. Mixed-mode Java-template integration (recommended)
approaches.description: Add tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 with LANGUAGE_PHP. Write php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class, interface, trait, enum), CALL_QUERY (function, member, nullsafe member, scoped calls), IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_declaration), REFERENCE_QUERY (named_type), DEFUSE_QUERY (parameters, assignments, augmented assignments, updates, variable reads), and a kind-checked extract_inheritance that walks base_clause and class_interface_clause children. Set extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver and find_receiver_type to None. Wire the registry as css does, and add the required tests.
pros: Meets every acceptance criterion in the issue, including the HTML-template case via LANGUAGE_PHP and the extends/implements case via the kind walk
Follows the java and swift template structure, so reviewers can compare directly
DEFUSE_QUERY supports the def-use analysis path that Java and Swift already expose
Mixed grammar handles real-world template files without an ERROR-node fallback
cons: DEFUSE pattern is the riskiest piece: the write/read dedup depends on match order, so an exact-count test is needed
Inheritance cannot reuse java.rs field lookups, so it is a new kind-based walk
Eight files touched, including a new integration test and README edits

approaches.name: B. Minimal surface: elements, calls and imports only
approaches.description: Same crate and registry wiring as A, but php.rs ships only ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY and IMPORT_QUERY, with REFERENCE_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance left None. This is the smallest change that makes analyze_file return language 'php' with functions, classes and calls.
pros: Fewest moving parts; lowest chance of a query-compile failure breaking .php analysis
Quickest to a reviewable first PR
Avoids the defuse dedup risk entirely
cons: Fails the issue's inheritance acceptance criterion (extends/implements must be returned)
No DEFUSE_QUERY, so analyze_symbol returns empty for PHP (parser_elements.rs 850-852); the issue scope names all five constants
Would need a follow-up PR, which the maintainers' in-house process may not welcome

approaches.name: C. Tags-driven queries from upstream queries/tags.scm
approaches.description: Start from the grammar's queries/tags.scm, which already captures interface, trait, class, function, method, calls and class_interface_clause, and rename its @name/@definition.* captures to aptu's function, func_name, method_name, class and class_name captures. Route class_interface_clause through impl_query or impl_trait_query, and hand-add the enum_declaration pattern that tags.scm lacks.
pros: Reuses captures maintained upstream and ties the element set to the grammar's own tagging
Less hand-written node-kind knowledge for calls and references
cons: tags.scm has no enum_declaration pattern, so enum still needs hand-written work
Its capture names do not match parser_elements.rs, so either the queries are renamed or the consumer changes, which widens scope
impl_query and impl_trait_query carry Rust impl-block semantics, so reusing them for implements misleads the consumers
Still needs a kind-based inheritance handler, so it does not remove the hardest part

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that meets all of the issue's acceptance criteria, which are the HTML-template case, extends/implements, the five query constants and the def-use path. It uses the mixed-mode LANGUAGE_PHP entry point, because php_only lacks the text kind that inline HTML needs. Before wiring, compile-test every query against LANGUAGE_PHP, which catches any stray `(identifier)` pattern early, and keep DEFUSE_QUERY as its own test target because it is the riskiest piece. Use the css wiring pattern verbatim, and pin tree-sitter-php to 0.25.2 after confirming its crates.io publish date is at least 7 days old.

inheritance_walk_citation: Source: tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php, php/grammar.js delegates to common/define-grammar.js (fetched via gh api). (1) class_declaration is prec.right(seq(optional(field('attributes', attribute_list)), repeat(_modifier), keyword('class'), field('name', reserved('classes', name))), optional(base_clause), optional(class_interface_clause), field('body', declaration_list))). So node.child_by_field_name("name") returns the `name` node; base_clause and class_interface_clause have NO field name and must be found by child.kind(). (2) base_clause: seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name)). Its children per node-types.json are name | qualified_name | relative_name (the _name choice; static and cast-type keywords are aliased to name). Walk: for each child of class_declaration with kind == "base_clause", for each named child with kind in {name, qualified_name, relative_name}, push format!("extends {text}"). (3) class_interface_clause: seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name)); same child kinds; walk: for each child with kind == "class_interface_clause", push format!("implements {text}") for each named child of kind name | qualified_name | relative_name. (4) interface_declaration: optional(base_clause) with no implements clause, so extends-only; enum_declaration: optional(class_interface_clause) so implements-only; trait_declaration: no clauses. Contrast with java.rs: Java uses child_by_field_name("superclass") and child_by_field_name("interfaces"); PHP has neither field, so the Java field-based walk cannot be copied. Text should come from get_node_text (languages/mod.rs) to avoid unchecked slicing. Qualified names keep their backslashes (e.g. \App\Base).
